# Codex -> llama-server on the host. Copied to ~/.codex/config.toml at build time.
# The host is reachable as host.docker.internal, never 127.0.0.1, from inside a container.

# These top-level keys MUST stay above the [model_providers.*] header,
# or TOML folds them into that table instead.
model_provider = "llamacpp"
model = "local"               # fallback only: the codex wrapper reads the served model from /v1/models
model_context_window = 32768  # fallback only: the codex wrapper reads the real n_ctx from /props

[model_providers.llamacpp]
name = "llama.cpp"
base_url = "http://host.docker.internal:9931/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
# No env_key: a keyless local endpoint is a first-class case for Codex.
# If your llama-server needs a key, add env_key = "MY_VAR" and set MY_VAR in .env.
----

# Codex ↔ llama-server: how it fits together

The source project's README → *Codex and llama-server* and *Model-specific considerations*
are the full account. This is the map, the things that look like errors and are not, and the probes.

## Moving parts

- `codex-config.toml` → `~/.codex/config.toml` at build time. `model` and `model_context_window`
  there are **fallbacks only**.
- `codex-wrapper.sh` → `~/.local/bin/codex`, ahead of `/usr/local/bin/codex`. At launch it reads
  `/v1/models` (model id) and `/props` (per-slot `n_ctx`) and passes `-c` overrides. Values are
  read once per launch. `specstory run codex` also goes through it.
- `seccomp.json` (via `runArgs`) → lets bubblewrap create user namespaces so Codex's sandbox
  works. Regenerate with `make-seccomp.sh`; it is Docker's default + `unshare clone mount
  umount2 pivot_root setns`.
- `patch-chat-template.sh` → host-side fix for templates that reject Codex's mid-conversation
  `developer` messages. Output goes to `--chat-template-file` on the host.

## Failure modes seen so far

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Host log: repeated 500 with *Jinja Exception: System message must be at the beginning*; Codex says *high demand* | Codex injected a `developer` message after user turns (e.g. after a command approval); Qwen3.8 template raises | `patch-chat-template.sh`, restart llama-server with the output |
| `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace` / *needs access to create user namespaces* | Docker default seccomp blocks `unshare`/`mount`/`pivot_root` | `seccomp.json` in `runArgs`; needs recreate |
| Codex thinks context is 32768 while server has more | Wrapper not on PATH, or server unreachable at launch | `which codex` must be `~/.local/bin/codex`; restart Codex |

## Not errors

- `Model metadata for '<model>' not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata` — the model isn't
  in Codex's compiled-in OpenAI catalog. Unfixable without lying about the model name; harmless
  since the wrapper supplies the context window.
- `unsupported Responses tool type 'namespace' skipped` / `'web_search'` in the server log —
  Codex tool types llama-server doesn't implement. Nothing to do with Linux namespaces.
- *"Codex's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap…"* — same as the bwrap row above, before the recreate.

## Probes (from inside the container)

```bash
curl -s $LLAMA_SERVER_URL/v1/models | jq -r .data[0].id                  # model id the wrapper passes
curl -s $LLAMA_SERVER_URL/props | jq .default_generation_settings.n_ctx   # context the wrapper passes
curl -s $LLAMA_SERVER_URL/props | jq -r .chat_template | grep -n raise_exception   # template guards
codex exec -s read-only "Reply with the single word OK"                   # end-to-end (not --json: waits on stdin)
unshare -Ur true && codex sandbox -- true && echo sandbox-ok              # sandbox works
```

The four-shape Responses probe for message-ordering failures is in the README →
*Model-specific considerations*. To see what Codex actually sent:

```bash
f=$(ls -t ~/.codex/sessions/*/*/*/rollout-*.jsonl | head -1)
jq -c 'select(.type=="response_item") | .payload | {type, role}' "$f"          # roles in order
jq -c 'select(.type=="event_msg") | .payload | select(.type=="token_count") | .info.model_context_window' "$f" | tail -1
```

Codex reports `model_context_window` minus its own reserve (98304 → 93388, 32768 → 31129).

--
104:### Codex's Linux sandbox
105-
106:Codex runs commands inside a bubblewrap sandbox, which needs unprivileged user namespaces.
107:Docker's default seccomp profile blocks the syscalls involved (`unshare`, `mount`,
108:`pivot_root`, …), so out of the box Codex warns *"Codex's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap and
109-needs access to create user namespaces"* and every command needs escalation.
110-
111:The container therefore runs with `.devcontainer/seccomp.json`: Docker's default profile with
112-exactly those syscalls allowed unconditionally — nothing else is loosened. Verify from inside:
113-
114-```bash
115:unshare -Ur true && codex sandbox -- true && echo sandbox-ok
116-```
117-
118:`make-seccomp.sh` regenerates the file from the current upstream default profile; run it
119-when Docker's profile changes and commit the result. If you would rather not allow user
120:namespaces at all, remove the `seccomp=` line from `runArgs` and set
121:`sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in `config.toml` — the container is the sandbox then.
122-
123-Known issue, as of 2026-09-20: JetBrains IDEs fail to create the container with `Status 500:
124:Decoding seccomp profile failed: invalid character '/' looking for beginning of value`. Their
125-dev-container support passes `runArgs` to the engine API verbatim instead of reading the profile
126-file the way the `docker` CLI does — [IJPL-67749](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IJPL-67749),
127-open since March 2024. The devcontainer CLI (which VS Code and Codespaces use) hands `runArgs`
--
130:`seccomp=` line in `runArgs`; everything else will then work, except for Codex's sandbox — see
131-the previous paragraph for what to set instead.
132-
133-Two things you will see that are not errors:
--
433:- The seccomp profile allows unprivileged user namespaces so Codex can sandbox its commands.
434-  That is the same thing a stock Linux desktop allows, and the container's own boundary is
435-  unchanged, but it does expose the kernel's user-namespace code to whatever runs inside.
436:  See *Codex's Linux sandbox* for how to turn it back off.
437-
438-## Build performance
439-
--
443:- `seccomp.json` is a run-time option, not part of the image; changing it needs a container restart, not a rebuild.

```text
Based on the search results, I found relevant information about this issue:

## Overview

Codex's Bubblewrap Linux sandbox fails while trying to mount a fresh /proc with the error: "bwrap: Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not permitted"

## The Problem

Codex seems to have a fallback for environments where mounting a fresh /proc is not permitted, however, it failed to use the fallback because it wrongly identified as mounting /proc worked. As a result, Codex does not recognise the failure and does not fall back to running Bubblewrap without mounting a fresh /proc.

## Root Cause

This issue occurs in containerized environments (Docker/Podman) where Docker containers mask entries such as /proc/kcore, which prevents unprivileged processes from mounting a fresh /proc filesystem.

## Solutions

One approach normalizes complete, recognized bwrap error lines to the /newroot/proc wording understood by the pinned CLI, and preserves the failure status so Codex activates its own no-proc fallback.

This appears to be an active issue in the OpenAI Codex project being addressed through compatibility workarounds in Home Assistant's Codex integration.
```

````text
# GitHub Issue Summary: Codex Sandbox /proc Mounting Failure

## The Error
When running Codex CLI in a Podman container, Bubblewrap fails with: `"bwrap: Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not permitted"`

## Root Cause
Codex has a fallback mechanism for environments that cannot mount a fresh `/proc`. However, the failure detection logic was too strict—it specifically looked for the path `/newroot/proc` in error messages. Bubblewrap 0.12.0 on Fedora 44 reports the error differently, using `/proc` instead, causing Codex to incorrectly believe the mount succeeded.

## Broken Fallback
The fallback mechanism (running Bubblewrap without the `--proc /proc` flag) never activates because the detection function doesn't recognize the error:

```
fn is_proc_mount_failure(stderr: &str) -> bool {
    stderr.contains("Can't mount proc")
        && stderr.contains("/newroot/proc")  // <- Only accepts this path
        && (stderr.contains("Invalid argument")
            || stderr.contains("Operation not permitted")
            || stderr.contains("Permission denied"))
}
```

## Version Affected
Codex CLI 0.153.4 (and likely earlier versions with similar detection logic)

## Proposed Solutions
The issue reporter suggests either removing the path check entirely or accepting both path formats (`/newroot/proc` or `on /proc`). A regression test is also proposed to prevent recurrence.

## Current Status
No linked pull requests or workarounds are mentioned in the issue content.
````
</details></tool-use>

```text
    /// Inherited fallback mounts that must be authenticated before sandboxed code runs.
    #[arg(long = "verify-fd-mount", hide = true)]
    pub verify_fd_mounts: Vec<String>,

    /// When set, skip mounting a fresh `/proc` even though PID isolation is
    /// still enabled. This is primarily intended for restrictive container
    /// environments that deny `--proc /proc`.
    #[arg(long = "no-proc", default_value_t = false)]
    pub no_proc: bool,

    /// Full command args to run under the Linux sandbox helper.
    // SAFETY: `read_fd` is a valid owned fd in the parent.
    let mut read_file = unsafe { File::from_raw_fd(read_fd) };
    let mut stderr_bytes = Vec::new();
    let mut limited_reader = (&mut read_file).take(MAX_PREFLIGHT_STDERR_BYTES);
    if let Err(err) = limited_reader.read_to_end(&mut stderr_bytes) {
        panic!("failed to read bubblewrap stderr: {err}");
    }

    let status = wait_for_bwrap_child(pid);
    let cleanup_signal_mask = ForwardedSignalMask::block();
    BWRAP_CHILD_PID.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);
    cleanup_synthetic_mount_targets(&synthetic_mount_registrations);
    cleanup_protected_create_targets(&protected_create_registrations);
    signal_forwarders.restore();
    cleanup_signal_mask.restore();
    if libc::WIFSIGNALED(status) {
        exit_with_wait_status(status);
    }

    String::from_utf8_lossy(&stderr_bytes).into_owned()
}

/// Close an owned file descriptor and panic with context on failure.
///
/// We use explicit close() checks here (instead of ignoring return codes)
/// because this code runs in low-level sandbox setup paths where fd leaks or
/// close errors can mask the root cause of later failures.
fn close_fd_or_panic(fd: libc::c_int, context: &str) {
    let close_res = unsafe { libc::close(fd) };
    if close_res < 0 {
        let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
        panic!("{context}: {err}");
    }
}
```

```text
bubblewrap (0.12.0-1~deb13u1) trixie-security; urgency=high

  * Merge new upstream release from unstable
    - Prevent sandbox escape via symlink traversal.
      If an app framework such as Flatpak mounts subdirectories into a
      directory controlled by the sandboxed app, a malicious or compromised
      sandboxed app could create symlinks in that directory to arrange for
      files/directories to be created on the host system.
      (GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx, no known CVE ID; Closes: #1145655)
    - bubblewrap no longer supports running when setuid, matching the
      upstream default. This ensures that vulnerabilities similar to
      CVE-2026-41163 can't happen in future.
  * Debian 13 backport changes:
    - d/control, d/gbp.conf: Branch for Debian 13 stable updates
    - Revert packaging changes that are not appropriate for a stable release
  * Packaging changes since 0.11.0-2+deb13u1:
    - d/rules: Stop passing -Dsupport_setuid=false.
      The option no longer exists, and the new version of bubblewrap always
      behaves as though its value was false.
    - d/rules: Don't compile fallback code paths for kernel older than 5.10.
```

```bash
head -5 .devcontainer/codex-wrapper.sh && cat > .devcontainer/bwrap-shim.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Volkert de Buisonjé <volkertb@users.noreply.github.com>
# SPDX-FileContributor: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

# Installed as /usr/local/bin/bwrap, ahead of /usr/bin/bwrap on PATH, so Codex's Linux
# sandbox finds it first.
#
# Codex asks bubblewrap for a fresh procfs (`--proc /proc`). Docker masks parts of the
# container's /proc (/proc/kcore, /proc/sys, ...), and the kernel then refuses to mount a
# new procfs from an unprivileged user namespace: "Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not
# permitted". Codex has a fallback for exactly this (`--no-proc`), but it recognises the
# failure only by bubblewrap's pre-0.12 wording ("/newroot/proc"); Debian 13 ships 0.12.0.
# See https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44329.
#
# This shim makes the same decision Codex would: if the kernel refuses a fresh procfs, drop
# `--proc <dest>` and run the sandbox with the container's /proc instead. Everything else
# (user/pid/ipc/net namespaces, read-only or tmpfs root, cap-drop, seccomp) is untouched,
# and the real bubblewrap is exec'd so PIDs, signals and inherited fds are unchanged.
# Remove this file once Codex detects the new wording.
set -euo pipefail

real=/usr/bin/bwrap

want_proc=false
for arg in "$@"; do
  [[ "$arg" == "--" ]] && break
  [[ "$arg" == "--proc" ]] && want_proc=true
done

if [[ "$want_proc" == true ]] \
   && ! "$real" --unshare-user --unshare-pid --ro-bind / / --proc /proc -- /bin/true 2>/dev/null; then
  args=()
  skip=false
  for arg in "$@"; do
    if [[ "$skip" == true ]]; then skip=false; continue; fi
    if [[ "$arg" == "--proc" ]]; then skip=true; continue; fi
    args+=("$arg")
  done
  exec "$real" "${args[@]}"
fi

exec "$real" "$@"
EOF
chmod 0755 .devcontainer/bwrap-shim.sh && shellcheck .devcontainer/bwrap-shim.sh && echo shellcheck-ok
cp .devcontainer/bwrap-shim.sh ~/.local/bin/bwrap && which bwrap
echo "== raw sandbox"; /usr/local/bin/codex sandbox -- sh -c 'echo pid=$$; ls /proc | grep -c "^[0-9]"' && echo sandbox-ok
echo "== read-only enforced"; /usr/local/bin/codex sandbox -- touch /workspaces/agentic-devcontainer/.sbx 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "== workspace-write"; /usr/local/bin/codex sandbox -c 'sandbox_mode="workspace-write"' -- sh -c 'touch /workspaces/agentic-devcontainer/.sbx && echo ws-write-ok && rm /workspaces/agentic-devcontainer/.sbx; touch /home/vscode/.sbx 2>&1 | tail -1; curl -s -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "net=%{http_code}\n" http://host.docker.internal:9931/v1/models || echo net-blocked'
```

```text
    rm -f ss.tgz ss.sha

# Codex CLI: static musl binary from the openai/codex GitHub release.
# Upstream publishes no .sha256, so the digests are pinned here and must be
# updated together with CODEX_VERSION:
#   curl -fsSL <asset-url> | sha256sum
RUN set -eux; \
    case "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" in \
      amd64) CODEX_TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl;  CODEX_SHA="${CODEX_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) CODEX_TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl; CODEX_SHA="${CODEX_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "No Codex binary for $(dpkg --print-architecture); skipping."; exit 0 ;; \
    esac; \
    cd /tmp; \
    curl -fsSL -o codex.tgz \
      "https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/download/rust-v${CODEX_VERSION}/codex-${CODEX_TARGET}.tar.gz"; \
    echo "${CODEX_SHA}  codex.tgz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    tar xzf codex.tgz; \
    mv "codex-${CODEX_TARGET}" /usr/local/bin/codex; \
    chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/codex; \
    rm -f codex.tgz

# Privilege hardening, last so it also strips anything the steps above installed.
# Default strips every setuid/setgid bit and locks root, leaving no in-container path to root.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt/lists,sharing=locked \
    set -eux; \
    if [ "${ALLOW_SUDO}" = "true" ]; then \
      apt-get update; \
      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends sudo; \
      echo "${USERNAME} ALL=(root) NOPASSWD:ALL" > "/etc/sudoers.d/${USERNAME}"; \
      chmod 0440 "/etc/sudoers.d/${USERNAME}"; \
    else \
      apt-get purge -y sudo || true; \
      rm -rf /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d /usr/bin/sudo /usr/bin/doas /usr/local/bin/sudo; \
      passwd -l root; \
      find / -xdev -perm /6000 -type f -exec chmod ug-s {} +; \
    fi

# Points Codex at the host's llama-server. Edit this file to change model or endpoint.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} codex-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.codex/config.toml

# `codex` on PATH resolves to this wrapper (~/.local/bin precedes /usr/local/bin below),
# which passes llama-server's actual context size to the real binary at launch.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} --chmod=0755 codex-wrapper.sh /home/${USERNAME}/.local/bin/codex

# Default lives here, not in containerEnv, so .env (docker --env-file) can override it.
# Codex itself reads config.toml; this is for ad-hoc checks and other tools.
ENV LLAMA_SERVER_URL=http://host.docker.internal:9931 \
    PATH=/home/${USERNAME}/.local/bin:${PATH}

USER ${USERNAME}

## 2026-09-20 — Wrapper passes model/context to Codex instead of hard-coding

Codex cannot query a custom provider and `config.toml` cannot compute values. A PATH-shadowing
wrapper with `-c` overrides was the only way to keep the config in sync with the server; the
config values remain as fallbacks for when the server is down at launch.

## 2026-09-20 — Chat-template fix is a generator script, not a committed template

The template is model-specific and comes from the running server; committing one would go
stale and imply the container is Qwen-specific. The script's workflow is model-neutral; the
per-model patch table is the only model-specific part.

## 2026-09-20 — `model = "local"` kept although the server ignores it

Single-model llama-server ignores the `model` field. Kept as the fallback for when the wrapper
cannot reach the server at launch.

## Earlier (from git history)

- No root, no sudo, setuid stripped, `no-new-privileges`: the agent runs confined to `vscode`;
  root work is done via `docker exec -u root` from the host. (README → *Working as root*)
- Codex checksums pinned in the Dockerfile, not exposed as build args, so version and digest
  can't drift apart. (README → *Download verification*)
- Everything installed at build time; no `postCreateCommand`, so container creation is offline.
```

````text
A Responses-shaped object back means the integration surface is good; then just run `codex`.
For a one-off test against a different endpoint without editing the config,
`CODEX_OSS_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:9931/v1` overrides Codex's built-in OSS provider.

### Codex's Linux sandbox

Codex runs commands inside a bubblewrap sandbox, which needs unprivileged user namespaces.
Docker's default seccomp profile blocks the syscalls involved (`unshare`, `mount`,
`pivot_root`, …), so out of the box Codex warns *"Codex's Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap and
needs access to create user namespaces"* and every command needs escalation.

The container therefore runs with `.devcontainer/seccomp.json`: Docker's default profile with
exactly those syscalls allowed unconditionally — nothing else is loosened. Verify from inside:

```bash
unshare -Ur true && codex sandbox -- true && echo sandbox-ok
```

`make-seccomp.sh` regenerates the file from the current upstream default profile; run it
when Docker's profile changes and commit the result. If you would rather not allow user
namespaces at all, remove the `seccomp=` line from `runArgs` and set
`sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in `config.toml` — the container is the sandbox then.

Known issue, as of 2026-09-20: JetBrains IDEs fail to create the container with `Status 500:
Decoding seccomp profile failed: invalid character '/' looking for beginning of value`. Their
dev-container support passes `runArgs` to the engine API verbatim instead of reading the profile
file the way the `docker` CLI does — [IJPL-67749](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IJPL-67749),
open since March 2024. The devcontainer CLI (which VS Code and Codespaces use) hands `runArgs`
to `docker run` unchanged, and the `docker` CLI reads the file itself, so those should be fine —
not yet confirmed by an actual run. To stay in JetBrains until it is fixed, comment out the
`seccomp=` line in `runArgs`; everything else will then work, except for Codex's sandbox — see
the previous paragraph for what to set instead.

Two things you will see that are not errors:

- `Model metadata for '<model>' not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata` at startup. Codex
  keeps a built-in table of per-model metadata (context window, reasoning support, truncation
  policy) keyed by OpenAI model names; a local model is not in it, so generic fallbacks apply.
  The context window is the one value that matters, and it is supplied separately (see below).
  The model name itself does not have to match the server's: a llama-server serving one model
  ignores the `model` field entirely, which is why the `curl` above works with `"model":"local"`.
- `unsupported Responses tool type 'namespace' skipped` (and `'web_search'`) in the server log.
  llama-server drops the Codex tool types it does not implement and carries on.

### Model and context window

Codex cannot ask a provider what it serves or how large its context is — its model metadata
is a static catalog of OpenAI models — and `config.toml` cannot compute values. So `codex` on
`PATH` is a wrapper (`.devcontainer/codex-wrapper.sh`, installed as `~/.local/bin/codex`,
ahead of the real binary) that asks llama-server at launch and passes the answers as
command-line overrides:
````

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-20 17:43:01Z)**_

## What's going on

Your two moats aren't fundamentally at odds — this is a three-week-old regression, and the evidence chain is solid:

- The seccomp fix worked. `unshare -Ur` and plain `bwrap` both succeed now. The failure moved one step further: `bwrap: Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not permitted`.
- Cause: Codex asks bubblewrap for a fresh procfs. Docker masks parts of `/proc` (tmpfs over `/proc/kcore`, `/proc/keys`…, read-only binds over `/proc/sys`, `/proc/bus`…), and the kernel refuses a new procfs from an unprivileged user namespace when the existing one has such overmounts (`mount_too_revealing`). I reproduced it with `unshare -Urm --mount-proc` too.
- Codex knows about this. It has a `--no-proc` fallback built for "restrictive container environments", triggered by a preflight that string-matches bubblewrap's error. That match still requires the substring `/newroot/proc` — on `main` as of today ([`linux_run_main.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs), `is_proc_mount_failure`). Bubblewrap 0.12.0 (2026-08-26) changed the wording to `on /proc`, and Debian pushed 0.12.0 to trixie-security (a sandbox-escape fix), so every Debian 13 image rebuilt since gets it. Codex issue [#44329](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44329) was filed 2026-09-09, is open, unfixed in 0.155.1 (the latest stable). A downstream project hit the identical thing ([moryoav/home-assistant-codex#9](https://github.com/moryoav/home-assistant-codex/issues/9), [PR #10](https://github.com/moryoav/home-assistant-codex/pull/10)).

Options I ruled out:
- `--security-opt systempaths=unconfined` — Docker's remedy; unmasks `/proc` for the whole container. That's the outer moat you didn't want to touch.
- `use_legacy_landlock` (Landlock-only, no namespaces) — tested, it panics under `workspace-write` in 0.155.1, and Codex's own `exec` run confirmed every command dies.

## What `--no-proc` costs — measured, not from the comments

The sandbox is *not* disabled. I ran the equivalent bwrap invocation with and without `--proc`:

| Still enforced without `--proc` | Lost |
|---|---|
| user, PID, IPC, network namespaces (`net=000`) | fresh procfs: `ps` inside shows the container's PIDs |
| read-only / tmpfs root, writable-roots list (`$HOME` denied in workspace-write) | other container processes' `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` readable |
| `--cap-drop ALL` (`CapEff: 0`), Codex's inner seccomp stage | |
| `/proc/<outer pid>/root`, `cwd`, `environ` and `kill` all blocked by the user namespace | |

So the leak is "see the container's process list and command lines" — same container, same uid. Filesystem masking is intact, which is the part that matters.

## The fix

`.devcontainer/bwrap-shim.sh`, installed as `/usr/local/bin/bwrap` (Codex resolves `bwrap` via `PATH`; it's placed in `/usr/local/bin` rather than `~/.local/bin` because Codex skips a `bwrap` found under the cwd, which `~` can be). It makes exactly the decision Codex's fallback would: probe once, drop `--proc <dest>` if the kernel refuses it, `exec /usr/bin/bwrap` with everything else untouched. Verified end-to-end: `codex exec -s workspace-write` with `approval_policy: never` (no escalation possible) created a file in the workspace; read-only and `$HOME` denial and network cut-off all hold. Nothing in `devcontainer.json`/Docker changed.

Also updated: Dockerfile (`COPY` line), README → *Codex's Linux sandbox* (new verification commands run as written), `codex-llama-server.md` (moving parts + failure-modes row + probe), `verifying-changes.md`, `decisions.md`, the layout list.

**Needs a rebuild** to land in the image — I can't verify that from here. Meanwhile a copy sits at `~/.local/bin/bwrap`, so Codex in your current container already works; the rebuild wipes that and installs the real one. Post-rebuild check: `which bwrap` → `/usr/local/bin/bwrap`, then the two commands from the README section.

One note: bubblewrap isn't in the Dockerfile's apt list — it comes with the base image. The shim hardcodes `/usr/bin/bwrap`, so if you want that explicit, add `bubblewrap` to the apt line. Say the word and I'll commit.

Sources: [openai/codex#44329](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44329), [moryoav/home-assistant-codex#9](https://github.com/moryoav/home-assistant-codex/issues/9), [moryoav/home-assistant-codex PR #10](https://github.com/moryoav/home-assistant-codex/pull/10), [bubblewrap v0.12.0 release](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/releases/tag/v0.12.0), [LKML: unprivileged proc mounts when not fully visible](https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/1804.0/02051.html)

Committed as `c9e4edd` (author set per-commit to the identity on your earlier commits, since no `~/.gitconfig` exists in the container — nothing global was written).

**Rebuild with the devcontainer CLI**, from the host, in the project folder:

```bash
devcontainer up --workspace-folder . --remove-existing-container
```

`--remove-existing-container` is what forces the rebuild; plain `devcontainer up` reuses the running container and won't pick up the Dockerfile change. Add `--build-no-cache` only if you want a from-scratch build (not needed here — the `COPY` layer is after the toolchain, so the cached layers are reused and it's quick).

Before you run it: `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` are discarded by a rebuild — the routine in `.devcontainer/agent_docs/session-continuity.md` covers what to save. Zed should re-attach to the new container the same way it did last time.

After it's up, from inside:

```bash
which bwrap                                   # /usr/local/bin/bwrap
unshare -Ur true && codex sandbox -- true && echo sandbox-ok
codex sandbox -c 'sandbox_mode="workspace-write"' -- sh -c 'touch .sbx && rm .sbx && touch ~/.sbx' # first ok, second denied
```

Then a real Codex session should run commands with no "Sandbox hiccup" and no escalation prompts for ordinary reads/writes in the workspace.

````text
**Before rebuilding the container, run `specstory sync`.** Agent state lives in the container's
home — `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` — and is not mounted, so it is lost on rebuild. `sync` writes
every Claude Code and Codex session for this directory to `.specstory/history/`, which is on
your host. To be able to *resume* a session afterwards rather than just read it, also copy the
raw transcripts out and back:

```bash
cp -a ~/.claude/projects .claude-backup/                 # before the rebuild (git-ignored)
cp -a .claude-backup/projects ~/.claude/ && claude --resume   # after
```

**Before committing `.specstory/history/`, read it.** Transcripts can contain keys, paths and
internal detail. Only `.specstory/debug/` is git-ignored by default.

== continuity doc lines 8-20

Nothing under the container user's home is mounted. A rebuild or recreate discards:

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl` | Claude Code transcripts (what `claude --resume` needs) |
| `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` | Claude Code's persistent memory for this project |
| `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, settings | Login — must log in again after a rebuild |
| `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` | Codex transcripts |
| `~/.codex/*.sqlite`, `~/.codex/rules/` | Codex state, approved-command rules |

The workspace folder is a bind mount and survives.
````
